sentences.text: Aspidichthys was a large, shield-like placoderm fish, a type of armored fish, featuring distinct bumps on its skin. Its thick bones were covered with an irregular pattern of large, rounded bumps.

The median dorsal plate of the type species A. clavatus measures between 39 and 44 centimeters in length. In contrast, the species A. ingens possesses an 80-centimeter-long nuchal plate that is folded more steeply than that of A. clavatus.
According to Dennison (1978), A. ingens is the largest arthrodire known from Europe due to its massive nuchal plate.
A 1938 restoration by Schmidt depicted A. ingens as having a large body, a small head, and enormous eye sockets based on a lost holotype.
The genus Aspidichthys was first described by Newberry in 1873.
The type species A. clavatus is known from fragments found in the Frasnian-aged Huron and Olentangy Shales of Ohio.
Aspidichthys belongs to the parent group Arthrodira and is classified within the class Placodermi.
The exact taxonomic classification of Aspidichthys remains uncertain among scientists.
Fossils of Aspidichthys date to the Frasnian stage of the Devonian period.
Aspidichthys lived from the Frasnian to the Famennian stages, approximately 382.31 to 358.86 million years ago.
The relationship between Aspidichthys and holonematids is considered doubtful because holonematid dorsal plates are narrower, have a low keel, and lack a carinal process.
